trial_title: Accuracy of Left Subclavian Regurgitation Evaluated by Ultrasound Doppler and 4D Flow MRI
brief_summary:
Aortic insufficiency (IA) is defined as an abnormal regurgitation of blood from the aorta to the left ventricle in diastole, due to a lack of tightness of the aortic valves. It represents about 10% of valvular pathologies but the annual mortality of nonoperated patients can be as high as 10% to 20%. The quantification of AI is therefore important as it can remain perfectly asymptomatic for a long time.

eligibility_table.criterion: Patient able to give informed consent to participate in the study
eligibility_table.justification: The patient is capable of giving informed consent as there is no indication of cognitive impairment.

eligibility_table.criterion: Patient with transthoracic echocardiography and MRI prescription
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has undergone multiple cardiac evaluations, suggesting that transthoracic echocardiography and MRI are likely prescribed.
There is no information provided about any contraindications to MRI; further details are needed.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have any implanted devices or metallic foreign bodies that would contraindicate an MRI?

eligibility_table.criterion: Pathologies of the thoracic aorta (aneurism, dissection, stenosis)
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has severe aortic stenosis and a dilated ascending aorta, which qualifies as pathologies of the thoracic aorta.

eligibility_table.criterion: Pathologies of the left subclavian artery (stenosis, narrowing)
eligibility_table.justification: There is no specific mention of pathologies of the left subclavian artery; further imaging results would clarify this.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Is there evidence of ≥50% stenosis in the left subclavian artery as assessed by ultrasound Doppler or 4D Flow MRI?

eligibility_table.justification: There is no information provided regarding the presence of a persistent arterial canal; further details are needed.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have a persistent arterial canal as confirmed by ultrasound Doppler or 4D Flow MRI?

eligibility_table.criterion: Arteriovenous fistula of the upper limb
eligibility_table.justification: There is no information provided regarding the presence of an arteriovenous fistula of the upper limb; further details are needed.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have an arteriovenous fistula of the upper limb confirmed by ultrasound Doppler or 4D Flow MRI?
